chunks: My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) who said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us who said: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab narrated to us, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Malik, from Masma' ibn Malik, from Sama'ah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said:

O Sama'ah! The believer is never free from four traits: a neighbor who annoys him, a devil who misleads him, a hypocrite who follows in his footsteps, and a believer who envies him. Then he said: O Sama'ah! Indeed, the worst of them for him is the jealous believer. I said: How is that? He said: He speaks ill of him and people believe him.

key_terms.أَشَدُّهُمْ عَلَيْهِ: the most severe of them for him
key_terms.يَقْفُو أَثَرَهُ: follows in his footsteps / pursues his trail
key_terms.يَنْفَكُّ: is never free from / does not cease to have

ai.seo_question: What are the four constant trials a believer faces according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this hadith in *Al-Khisal*, emphasizing that spiritual resilience requires enduring not just external enemies but also internal community dynamics. The Imam identifies the envying believer as the most severe trial because their criticism carries the weight of credibility, making their falsehoods more damaging than the devil's whispers or the hypocrite's schemes. This highlights the Shia scholarly focus on *sirr* (inner state) and the psychological complexity of social interactions within the faithful community.
